name.en: “Dial *21*”: a fake bank caller makes you forward your calls

how.en: Someone claiming to be your bank calls, texts or emails about suspicious activity on your account or a security problem with your phone. They may already know your name and number. They try to get banking details or one-time passcodes, then tell you to open your dial pad and enter *21* followed by a number they give you, “to verify your device”. This turns on call forwarding: when your real bank rings to check a payment, the call goes to the criminal, who passes the security checks as you.

text.en: Someone claiming to be your bank contacts you about suspicious activity or a phone security issue.
They ask for your online banking details or a one-time passcode.
They tell you to type *21* and a number on your phone to “verify the device”.
They keep you on the phone so you can’t ring the bank yourself.

Caller: We’ve flagged some unusual logins on your account, so I need to secure this handset. Open your keypad and enter star two one star, then the number I read out, then hash and call. Stay on the line with me while it connects.

en: told to dial star 21 on my phone
caller asked me to enter a code with *21*
bank said to verify my device by dialling a code
my calls are being forwarded after a bank call
fake bank asked me to change my phone settings
Being asked to dial a code starting *21* or to change your phone’s settings: no bank asks for this.
A caller asking for a one-time passcode.
An unexpected call about your phone’s “security”.
Hang up. Ring your bank on the number on the back of your card.
If you dialled the code, call your bank and your mobile provider straight away so call forwarding is switched off.
Check your account for payments you don’t recognise and report it to the Gardaí.

sources.title: Fraud Alert: Do not dial *21* phone codes at the request of an unexpected caller
